items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: I had entered into a studio with Eddie Bearfield and Jimmy Mundy and myself, we were in a studio on 48th Street... and we called it BMJ, which is Bearfield, Mundy, Johnson, and we were going to try to set up an arranging and copying service

ctx.x: (Esa El-Sayee) was from Haiti, and he had come back to see Panama Francis because Panama Francis' father was a Haitian. And he came back to see Panama, and then so doing, I had the pleasure of meeting him. And he told me then, he says, Bud Johnson, he says, I sure like the way you play saxophone. He says, I play a little tenor saxophone myself. Can I take some lessons from you?

Well, I had entered into a studio with Eddie Bearfield and Jimmy Mundy and myself, we were in a studio on 48th Street between 6th and 7th Avenue in New York, and we called it BMJ, which is Bearfield, Mundy, Johnson, and we were going to try to set up an arranging and copying service and just write music for everybody. So he came up to the studio, and I used to do some teaching with him. So I mean I used to do some instructing for him, and when we got to know
